submission.natural_language_explanation: This pole fires retrospectively when the current token is a familiar, in-vocabulary word or number-fragment arriving as a contextually predictable step of a fluent conventional sequence: a memorized fact ('boils at 100'), an idiom or formulaic opening ('Once upon', 'Please'), boilerplate (an HTML closing tag, SQL 'ORDER', 'np' after its import), or a strong collocation ('greater than', 'light-years', 'contract was void'); its output direction generically promotes familiar word-suffix and completion fragments (Jacobian kurtosis 12.3) without preparing any specific token seen after the peaks. It is near-silent on fragments of unfamiliar names and identifiers (the negative pole's triggers, e.g. ' Sz'/'cz'/'ep' ~ 0), on sentence-initial 'The' with no preceding context, and weaker on tokens already fully fixed by the previous token ('upon' after 'Once', the second '0' in '100'); scrambling the preceding fluent context or swapping in an out-of-place token sharply lowers familiar content-word peaks, while changing only later tokens leaves the peak exactly unchanged.
